about.title: About GainWell
about.lead: A free library for people who want to eat more, built in English and French.
body: GainWell exists because gaining weight is harder than it looks. Full stomachs, low appetite, expensive food and vague advice all get in the way.
The plan is a small, quiet tool: recipes that are actually filling, guides that explain calories and protein in plain words, and a daily log that shows a trend rather than a verdict.
Today the public library is open. Accounts, profiles and tracking are being built, so nothing about you is stored yet.
GainWell is free, and it will stay free. It does not sell your data, and it does not advertise diets.
principles: No promised results. People gain weight at different speeds.
Metric units always: grams, millilitres, kilocalories.
Sample data is labelled sample data.
about.languagesBody: Every page is written in English and French. Numbers use metric units, and dates follow the language you chose.

howItWorks.title: How GainWell works
howItWorks.lead: Three steps, once accounts are open. Until then, the recipes and guides are yours to use.
howItWorks.step1Body: You give a starting weight, an appetite range and a weekly pace. GainWell turns that into a daily calorie line, never a fixed promise.
howItWorks.step2Body: Pick a recipe, cook it, and the meal lands in your day. Ingredients and quantities scale to the servings you made.
howItWorks.step3Body: A week of days sits side by side, so you can see whether you ate more or less than your line.
howItWorks.statusOpen: Open now: recipe library, guides, English and French, metric units.
howItWorks.statusBuilding: Being built: accounts, profiles, meal logs, daily targets.
howItWorks.statusNote: Nothing you write is stored yet, because there is no account system. This page describes what the tool will do.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: What this site stores about you today, in plain words.

sections.heading: Language preference
sections.body: When you switch to French or English, the site saves a small cookie called NEXT_LOCALE so your next visit opens in the same language. It holds a language code and nothing else.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.body: Accounts are open. Creating one stores your email address, an optional display name, your language choice and a couple of timestamps. Once you set up the nutrition profile it also stores the answers you typed: completed age in years (never a birthday), optional sex, height, current weight, activity level, eating habits, optional appetite and meals, dietary preference, allergies or foods you avoid, your goal, and optional target weight or a calorie target a professional gave you. Only you can read those answers, estimates are recalculated from them rather than stored, and no numbers are produced for an account under 18. The meal log and weight records arrive in a later stage under the same rules. To have your account deleted, write to hello@example.com until deletion ships in the app.

sections.heading: No analytics, no advertising
sections.body: This site does not use analytics tools or advertising trackers, and it does not sell or share data.

sections.heading: Recipe data
sections.body: Recipes and guides are written sample content stored in the site itself. They contain no personal information.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about privacy can be sent to hello@example.com. This address is a placeholder until the support inbox is set up.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: The short version: use the library freely, and treat the numbers as estimates.

sections.heading: Not medical advice
sections.body: GainWell gives general nutrition information. It is not a diagnosis, a treatment or a replacement for a doctor or dietitian. If you have a health condition, ask a professional before changing how you eat.

sections.heading: Sample content
sections.body: Recipes and guides are hand-written samples with estimated nutrition figures. They are not verified against a food database, and they may change as the real data arrives.

sections.heading: Your use
sections.body: You may read, cook and share the recipes for personal use. Do not scrape or resell the library, and do not present the estimates as verified data.

sections.heading: Accounts
sections.body: An account stores your email address, an optional display name and your language choice. The privacy page lists everything that is stored. Recipes remain sample content, and the numbers remain estimates.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: These terms change as the product grows. Each version is dated at the top of this page.

dashboard.title: Your dashboard
dashboard.macrosNote: The gram amounts use the standard conversion factors (4 kcal per g for protein and carbohydrate, 9 kcal per g for fat). The split itself is one simple product assumption, not a requirement. Rounded grams can differ from the target by a few kilocalories.
dashboard.highActivityNote: You chose the highest activity level GainWell offers. The estimate can still be too low for a genuinely vigorous lifestyle, so treat it as a starting point rather than a precise target.
dashboard.lowEstimateNote: This estimate is unusually low for an adult. It is the plain arithmetic result of the answers above — not a recommendation and not a sign that eating this little is safe. If it does not match your situation, a professional can help you read it.
dashboard.reconfirmNote: Your nutrition answers were last saved over a year ago. If anything has changed — your age included — updating them keeps the estimates honest.
dashboard.assumptions: Estimated with the Mifflin–St Jeor resting-energy equation and rounded activity bands, then adjusted conservatively. These are estimates for general education, not measurements and not medical advice.
dashboard.professionalNote: The daily target is the number you entered from your professional. GainWell shows it exactly as given, never clamps or replaces it, and does not check it; its own suggestion ({kcal} kcal) is beside it for comparison.
dashboard.professionalLowNote: A professional target this low is unusual for most adults. GainWell does not validate the numbers professionals give — confirming this one fits you is a conversation to have with the professional who gave it.
dashboard.recalculatedNote: Estimates are recalculated from your answers each time you edit them.
dashboard.minorBody: You are under 18, so GainWell does not calculate personal calorie or macronutrient targets — those adult numbers are not appropriate for younger people. Instead: eat regularly, include protein at each meal, and drink enough water.
dashboard.minorTalkTo: If you are worried about your weight, talk with a parent or guardian and a healthcare professional you trust. They can answer in a way that fits your body and your age.
dashboard.incompleteBody: Your nutrition profile is not finished, so GainWell has no answers to work from. It will not invent numbers.

onboarding.title: Set up your profile
onboarding.lead: Five short steps. GainWell uses your answers to estimate your daily energy. Nothing here is a diagnosis.

step1.title: About you
step1.lead: Your body measures, so the estimate is built from you rather than a generic number. Age is stored as completed years; a birthday is never asked for.

step2.title: Activity and eating habits
step2.lead: How much you move and how you eat today. Choose the description that fits best; a rough answer is enough.

step3.title: Dietary preferences
step3.lead: What you like to eat and what you avoid. This shapes recipe suggestions only, and you can clear it later.

step4.title: Your goal
step4.lead: Describe where you want to get to. GainWell stays gradual and never promises a pace of weight gain.

step5.title: Review
step5.lead: Check your answers before they are saved. Every step stays editable afterwards.

age.label: Age
age.hint: Completed years. Personal estimates require 18 or older; under 18 you get general guidance instead.

sex.hint: Optional. The resting-energy equation is sex-specific, so without this answer GainWell cannot produce numbers. Nothing is guessed from other answers. This asks about the body the equation models, not about gender identity.

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.hint: Exercise most days or regular walking

regular.label: Meals most days
regular.hint: You eat at roughly the same times each day

skipped_meals.label: Meals get skipped
skipped_meals.hint: Busy days often leave out a meal

low_appetite.label: Small appetite
low_appetite.hint: Full portions feel like a lot

varied.label: Varied
varied.hint: Meal times and sizes change day to day

appetite.hint: Your appetite tells GainWell how much food you can comfortably eat.

notes.label: Allergies or foods you avoid (optional)
notes.hint: In your own words. Used to keep recipe suggestions suitable, never to calculate numbers. Clear it by emptying this box.

gain_gradually.label: Gain weight gradually
gain_gradually.hint: A small, steady daily surplus; no promised pace

eating_consistency.label: Eat more consistently
eating_consistency.hint: Steadiness is the goal, so the target stays at maintenance

healthier_habits.label: Build healthier eating habits
healthier_habits.hint: Maintenance energy, with room to change habits

professional_guidance.label: Follow a target from a professional
professional_guidance.hint: Your professional's number wins; GainWell never overwrites it

targetWeight.label: Target weight (optional)
targetWeight.hint: A loose goal, not a commitment. Leave it empty if you prefer.

professional.label: Daily calorie target from a professional (optional)
professional.hint: If a doctor or dietitian gave you a number, put it here. It is stored separately and never replaced by GainWell's estimate.
